_comment: Schema reference for per-tool SEO content files. One file per slug at landing/tools_content/<slug>.json. This file itself is not a real tool and is excluded from generation.
intro: 2-4 sentences in plain clinical English explaining what the tool does, who uses it, and why it matters. Must be grounded in the source Dart screen's own info-card/description text, not invented.
indications: Bullet points: when/why a clinician would reach for this tool.

3-6 bullets. Derive from the tool's own purpose/subtitle/category — reasonable clinical inference is fine here (this is normal usage context, not a specific numeric/guideline claim), but do not state specific thresholds or guideline-sourced numbers unless they appear in the source file.
method: Plain-language description of the calculation/approach. If the source Dart file contains an explicit formula string (e.g. in a Text widget, comment, or callout box), quote it verbatim or near-verbatim. If no formula is present in source (e.g. a reference guide/algorithm screen), describe the tool's approach in general terms instead — do not invent a formula.
guidelineRefs: Only include a guideline/source name here if it is EXPLICITLY named in the source Dart file (e.g. 'AAP 2022', 'ESPGHAN 2022', 'Fenton 2013', 'NICHD', 'Second Task Force 1987'). Leave this array EMPTY if the source file names no specific guideline — never guess a year or body.

faqs.q: A realistic question a clinician or trainee would search or ask about this exact tool.
faqs.a: 1-3 sentence answer grounded in the source file's own content. No invented numeric thresholds.
Keep answers factual and traceable to the source screen's own text.

sourceFilesRead: Relative path(s) of the Dart file(s) actually read to write this content — for audit trail.
